a.title: .NET: Add AppBundleResourcePrefix property to unify resource prefix properties
a.body:
This PR unifies the various resource prefix properties (`IPhoneResourcePrefix`, `MonoMacResourcePrefix`, and `XamMacResourcePrefix`) into a single property (`AppBundleResourcePrefix`) for use in .NET projects.

The implementation:

1. Adds a new `AppBundleResourcePrefix` property in `Xamarin.Shared.props` with a default value of "Resources"
2. Updates the property precedence to use `AppBundleResourcePrefix` first, then fall back to the platform-specific properties
3. Maintains backward compatibility by having legacy properties default to the new property if they're not explicitly set
4. Updates comments in MSBuild files to reflect the changes
5. Updates documentation in `build-properties.md` to document the new property and add recommendations for using it instead of the legacy properties

Users can now specify a single resource prefix property that works across all platforms:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <AppBundleResourcePrefix>Resources</AppBundleResourcePrefix>
</PropertyGroup>
```

Legacy properties will continue to work for backward compatibility, but the new property is recommended for new .NET projects.

Fixes #12808.

a.title: Fix: TagHelperContext.AllAttributes missing attributes after Razor comment
a.body:
Fix: TagHelperContext.AllAttributes missing attributes after Razor comment ## Problem Analysis When a Razor comment (`@* *@`) appears in an element's attribute list, any attributes after it are missing from `TagHelperContext.AllAttributes`. The root cause was in `TagHelperBlockRewriter.cs`: 1. When iterating through `startTag.Attributes`, whitespace between attributes is represented as standalone `MarkupTextLiteralSyntax` nodes 2. These didn't match any known attribute types, causing `result = null` 3. a.title: Add conditional 16KB page size support for Android 15+ compliance
a.body:
- [x] Add conditional 16KB page size support for Android 15+ compliance
- [x] Fix RECORD_AUDIO permission lint error triggered by higher target SDK
  - Added RECORD_AUDIO permission to library AndroidManifest.xml
  - Added @SuppressLint("MissingPermission") annotation to AudioRecordRunnable constructor
  - Verified lint check passes and full build succeeds
- [x] Fix android:exported requirement for Android 15+ target SDK
  - Added android:exported="true" to MainActivity in AndroidManifest.xml
  - Required when targeting API 31+ (Android 15 uses API 35) for activities with intent filters
  - Verified build succeeds with and without 16KB page sizes enabled

## Overview

Google requires all apps targeting Android 15+ to support 16KB page sizes. While the project already had native library support for 16KB page sizes, it was missing the application-level configuration needed for the APK to actually enable 16KB page sizes on Android 15+ devices.

## Implementation

The solution adds conditional Android SDK targeting based on the existing `enable16kPageSizes` property in `local.properties`:

**When `enable16kPageSizes=true`:**
- App targets Android 15 (API level 35) for full 16KB page size support
- Native libraries built with `-DENABLE_16K_PAGE_SIZES=ON` (already implemented)
- APK will use 16KB page sizes on compatible Android 15+ devices

**When `enable16kPageSizes=false` or missing:**
- App targets API level 25 (existing default behavior)
- Standard 4KB page size behavior maintained
- Full backward compatibility preserved

## Changes Made

### Application Module (`cgeDemo/build.gradle`)
- Added `enable16kPageSizes()` function to read the property from gradle.ext
- Modified `targetSdkVersion` to conditionally use API 35 when 16KB page sizes are enabled:
  ```gradle
  targetSdkVersion enable16kPageSizes() ? 35 : rootProject.ext.android.targetSdkVersion
  ```

### Root Build Configuration (`build.gradle`)
- Updated `compileSdkVersion` from 30 to 35 to support Android 15 features

### Android Manifest Updates
- Added `android:exported="true"` to MainActivity in `cgeDemo/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
- Required when targeting API 31+ for activities with intent filters per Android security requirements

### Library Module Permission Fix
- Added `RECORD_AUDIO` permission to `library/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
- Added `@SuppressLint("MissingPermission")` annotation to `AudioRecordRunnable` constructor to handle stricter lint checks with higher target SDK

## Usage

Users can control the behavior via `local.properties`:

```properties
# Enable 16KB page sizes (targets Android 15)
enable16kPageSizes=true
usingCMakeCompile=true

# Disable 16KB page sizes (uses existing behavior)  
enable16kPageSizes=false
```

The implementation integrates seamlessly with the existing CLI tools:
```bash
# Enable via command line
bash tasks.sh --enable-16kb-page-size

# Disable via command line  
bash tasks.sh --disable-16kb-page-size
```

## Benefits

- **Android 15+ Compliance**: Meets Google's requirements for 16KB page size support
- **Backward Compatible**: Existing projects continue to work unchanged
- **Conditional**: Only enables 16KB page sizes when explicitly requested
- **Integrated**: Works with existing build system and tooling
- **Future-Proof**: Ready for Google Play Store requirements
- **Lint Clean**: All lint checks pass with proper permission handling
- **Manifest Compliant**: Meets Android security requirements for exported activities

This ensures the project can be published to Google Play Store for Android 15+ devices while maintaining compatibility with older Android versions.

b.title: Add automatic 16KB page size detection and status reporting to CGE library
b.body:
This PR implements comprehensive runtime detection for 16KB page size support in the CGE (Computer Graphics Engine) library to help developers verify Google Play Store compliance and debug configuration issues.

## Problem

Google requires all Android apps to support 16KB page sizes, but developers need visibility into whether their app is properly configured and functioning with 16KB pages. The 16KB page size feature is only truly supported on Android 15+ devices, creating multiple scenarios that need to be distinguished.

## Solution

Added automatic detection that runs during `JNI_OnLoad` when the CGE library loads, providing comprehensive status reporting with three levels of analysis:

### Detection Levels

1. **Compile-time Check**: Verifies if `ENABLE_16K_PAGE_SIZES` was defined during build
2. **Runtime System Check**: Confirms Android device supports 16KB pages (API 35+)  
3. **Active Usage Check**: Validates that 16KB pages are actually being used via `sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE)`

### Status Categories

The detection reports one of four clear states:

- **`DISABLED`**: 16KB support not enabled at compile time
- **`COMPILE_READY`**: Support compiled in but Android version < 35
- **`SUPPORTED_BUT_INACTIVE`**: All support available but 16KB pages not currently active
- **`ACTIVE`**: 16KB pages fully working

### Example Output

```
W/libCGE: === CGE 16KB Page Size Status ===
W/libCGE: Status: ACTIVE
W/libCGE: Details: 16KB page size is fully active and working
I/libCGE: Compile-time support: YES
I/libCGE: Android API Level: 35 (16KB support needs API 35+)
I/libCGE: Current page size: 16384 bytes
I/libCGE: 16KB pages active: YES
W/libCGE: ================================
```

## Implementation Details

- **Location**: `library/src/main/jni/interface/cgeNativeLibrary.cpp`
- **Function**: `cgeCheck16kPageSize()` called from `JNI_OnLoad()`
- **Dependencies**: Uses standard POSIX `sysconf()` and Android NDK `android_get_device_api_level()`
- **Logging**: Uses `CGE_LOG_KEEP` for critical status (visible in release builds)

## Configuration

To enable 16KB page size support:

```properties
# gradle.properties
gradle.ext.enable16kPageSizes = true
gradle.ext.usingCMakeCompile = true
```

## Benefits

- **Zero Integration Cost**: Runs automatically during library initialization
- **Clear Debugging**: Immediate visibility into 16KB page size configuration
- **Compliance Verification**: Helps ensure Google Play Store requirements are met
- **Multi-scenario Handling**: Distinguishes between compile-time, runtime, and active support

## Documentation

- Added comprehensive guide in `16KB_PAGE_SIZE_DETECTION.md`
- Updated README.md with feature overview
- Included configuration examples and troubleshooting information

This feature provides essential visibility for developers working with 16KB page sizes without requiring any changes to existing application code.

b.title: Add option to specify contact URI when making call (PJSUA and PJSUA2)
b.body:
This PR adds support for specifying a custom Contact URI when making SIP calls through both the PJSUA C API (`pjsua_call_make_call()`) and PJSUA2 C++ API, addressing issue #4584.

## Changes Made

### PJSUA (C API) Implementation
- **Added `contact_uri` field** to `pjsua_msg_data` structure in `pjsua.h`
- **Modified `pjsua_call_make_call()`** to prioritize `msg_data->contact_uri` when provided
- **Updated `pjsua_msg_data_clone()`** to properly duplicate the `contact_uri` field
- **Added URI validation** for both `contact_uri` and `local_uri` to prevent invalid URIs from being used

### PJSUA2 (C++ API) Implementation
- **Added `contactUri` field** to `SipTxOption` structure in `siptypes.hpp`
- **Updated `SipTxOption::toPj()`** to convert `contactUri` to `pjsua_msg_data.contact_uri`
- **Updated `SipTxOption::fromPj()`** to convert `pjsua_msg_data.contact_uri` to `contactUri`
- **Updated `SipTxOption::isEmpty()`** to include `contactUri` in the empty check

### Contact URI Priority Logic
The Contact header selection now follows this priority order:
1. `msg_data->contact_uri` (if provided and valid)
2. Account's configured contact (`acc->contact`)  
3. Auto-generated contact via `pjsua_acc_create_uac_contact()`

## Usage Examples

### PJSUA (C API)
```c
pjsua_msg_data msg_data;
pjsua_call_id call_id;

// Initialize message data
pjsua_msg_data_init(&msg_data);

// Set custom Contact URI
msg_data.contact_uri = pj_str("sip:mycustom@192.168.1.100:5060");

// Make call with custom Contact URI
status = pjsua_call_make_call(acc_id, 
                              &pj_str("sip:dest@example.com"),
                              NULL, NULL, &msg_data, &call_id);
```

### PJSUA2 (C++ API)
```cpp
CallOpParam prm;
prm.txOption.contactUri = "sip:mycustom@192.168.1.100:5060";

call->makeCall(dest_uri, prm);
```

## Verification

The implementation has been thoroughly tested:

- ✅ **Functional verification**: Custom Contact URI correctly appears in SIP INVITE messages (both C and C++ APIs)
- ✅ **Backward compatibility**: Existing code continues to work unchanged (empty `contact_uri`/`contactUri` uses default behavior)
- ✅ **Input validation**: Invalid URIs are rejected with `PJSIP_EINVALIDREQURI` error for both `contact_uri` and `local_uri`
- ✅ **Memory management**: Proper string duplication in clone operations
- ✅ **PJSUA2 conversion**: Bidirectional conversion between `SipTxOption` and `pjsua_msg_data` works correctly
- ✅ **Regression testing**: All existing PJSUA tests pass

## SIP Message Impact

**Before (default behavior):**
```
Contact: <sip:test@127.0.0.1:5060;ob>
```

**After (with custom contact_uri/contactUri):**
```
Contact: <sip:mycustom@192.168.1.100:5060>
```

This feature enables applications to specify different Contact URIs per call, which is useful for multi-homed systems, load balancing scenarios, and advanced SIP routing configurations. The feature is now available in both the C API (PJSUA) and C++ API (PJSUA2).

a.title: Add support for setting include paths via initializationParams
a.body:
This PR adds the ability to configure include paths dynamically through LSP `initializationParams`, addressing a key limitation for Neovim users where command-line arguments must be static but initialization options can be set dynamically.

## Problem

Neovim's LSP configuration requires `cmd` and `args` to be static, making it impossible to dynamically configure include paths based on project context. While Neovim supports changing `initializationParams` via the `before_init` callback, protols didn't support include path configuration through this mechanism.

## Solution

Extended the LSP initialization process to parse and use include paths from `initializationParams.include_paths`. The implementation:

- **Integrates seamlessly**: Merges with existing CLI and configuration file include paths  
- **Handles errors gracefully**: Invalid formats are logged but don't crash the server
- **Maintains compatibility**: All existing functionality continues to work unchanged

## Usage

Neovim users can now configure include paths dynamically:

```lua
require'lspconfig'.protols.setup{
  before_init = function(_, config)
    config.init_options = {
      include_paths = {
        "/usr/local/include/protobuf",
        "vendor/protos",
        "../shared-protos"
      }
    }
  end
}
```

## Implementation Details

- Extended `WorkspaceProtoConfigs` to store initialization include paths
- Added `parse_init_include_paths()` function to handle JSON parsing with robust error handling
- Updated include path resolution to merge all sources (config file + CLI + initialization)
- Added comprehensive test coverage with 6 new test cases
- Updated documentation with usage examples

## Testing

All existing tests continue to pass, plus new tests covering:
- Array format parsing
- String format parsing  
- Invalid format handling
- Integration with existing include path sources
- Real-world usage scenarios

Fixes #90.

## Changes Made

### 1. Updated Azure SDK Dependencies
- Updated `github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-go/sdk/azidentity` from v1.6.0 to v1.10.1
- Updated `github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-go/sdk/azcore` from v1.11.1 to v1.18.0
- Updated `github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-go/sdk/security/keyvault/azkeys` from v1.0.1 to v1.3.1

### 2. New Credential Types Implemented

The following new `fedauth` connection string parameter values are now supported:

- **`ActiveDirectoryAzureDeveloperCli`** - Authenticates using Azure Developer CLI credentials
- **`ActiveDirectoryEnvironment`** - Authenticates using environment variables (AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET)
- **`ActiveDirectoryWorkloadIdentity`** - Authenticates using workload identity for Kubernetes and other OIDC environments
- **`ActiveDirectoryAzurePipelines`** - Authenticates using Azure DevOps Pipelines service connections
  - Requires: `serviceconnectionid`, `systemtoken`, and `user id` parameters
- **`ActiveDirectoryClientAssertion`** - Authenticates using JWT client assertions
  - Requires: `clientassertion` and `user id` parameters
- **`ActiveDirectoryOnBehalfOf`** - Authenticates using the on-behalf-of flow for delegated access
  - Requires: `userassertion` and `user id` parameters
  - Supports client secret, certificate, or client assertion authentication

### 3. Documentation Updates

Updated the README.md with:
- Documentation for all new credential types with parameter descriptions
- Code examples showing how to use the new authentication methods
- Clear guidance on when each credential type should be used

### 4. Comprehensive Testing

Added extensive test coverage including:
- Connection string parsing tests for all new credential types
- Parameter validation tests ensuring proper error handling
- Negative test cases for missing required parameters

## Example Usage

```go
// Environment credential (uses AZURE_* environment variables)
db, err := sql.Open(azuread.DriverName, 
    "sqlserver://server.database.windows.net?database=mydb&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryEnvironment")

// Workload identity (for Kubernetes environments)
db, err := sql.Open(azuread.DriverName, 
    "sqlserver://server.database.windows.net?database=mydb&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryWorkloadIdentity")

// Azure Pipelines
connStr := "sqlserver://server.database.windows.net?database=mydb&fedauth=ActiveDirectoryAzurePipelines"
connStr += "&user+id=" + url.QueryEscape("client-id@tenant-id")
connStr += "&serviceconnectionid=connection-id&systemtoken=access-token"

```

b.title: Fix bulk insert failure with datetime values near midnight due to day overflow
b.body:
This PR fixes a bulk insert failure that occurs when inserting datetime values very close to midnight, specifically when the fractional seconds round up to the next second causing a day overflow.

## Problem

When performing a bulk insert using `mssql.CopyIn` into a datetime column, inserting a `time.Time` value very close to midnight causes the following error:

```
mssql: OLE DB provider 'STREAM' for linked server '(null)' returned invalid data for column '[!BulkInsert].CreateTime'.
```

The issue occurs with timestamps like `time.Date(2025, 1, 1, 23, 59, 59, 998_350_000, time.UTC)` where the fractional seconds (998.35ms) round to 300 three-hundredths of a second, which represents exactly 1 full second.

## Root Cause

The `encodeDateTime` function calculates the time portion as:
```go
tm := 300*(t.Second()+t.Minute()*60+t.Hour()*60*60) + nanosToThreeHundredthsOfASecond(t.Nanosecond())
```

For the problematic timestamp `23:59:59.998350000`:
- Base time: `300*(59 + 59*60 + 23*60*60) = 25,919,700`
- Fractional part: `nanosToThreeHundredthsOfASecond(998350000) = 300` (rounds up to 1 second)
- Total: `tm = 25,920,000` which equals exactly one full day worth of three-hundredths

This overflow into the next day was not handled, causing SQL Server to reject the encoded value as invalid.

## Solution

Added day overflow detection and handling in the `encodeDateTime` function:

```go
// Handle day overflow when time calculation exceeds one day
// One day = 86400 seconds = 86400 * 300 three-hundredths = 25,920,000
if tm >= 300*86400 {
    days++
    tm = tm - 300*86400
}
```

When the time portion overflows, we increment the day counter and wrap the time back to the beginning of the day, ensuring the encoded value represents the correct date and time after rounding.

## Testing

Added comprehensive tests covering:
- The original failing case (998.35ms before midnight)
- Various boundary conditions near midnight
- Edge cases with maximum date ranges  
- Bulk copy parameter generation
- Round-trip encoding/decoding verification

All existing tests continue to pass, confirming backward compatibility.

## Example

```go
// This now works without error
data := time.Date(2025, 1, 1, 23, 59, 59, 998_350_000, time.UTC)
stmt, _ := db.Prepare(mssql.CopyIn("TestTable", mssql.BulkOptions{}, "CreateTime"))
stmt.Exec(data) // Successfully rounds to 2025-01-02 00:00:00
```

Fixes #270.

a.title: Fix Go code quality issues in cmd/generate package: resource leaks, variable shadowing, and error handling
a.body:
This PR addresses several critical Go code quality issues identified in the `cmd/generate` package, focusing on resource management, variable shadowing, and proper error handling.

## Issues Fixed

### 🔴 Critical Resource Management Issues
Fixed resource leaks in `cmd/generate/llm.go` where `defer` statements inside retry loops caused spinners and readers to accumulate without proper cleanup:

**Before:**
```go
for attempt := 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++ {
    sp := spinner.New(...)
    sp.Start()
    defer sp.Stop()  // ❌ Multiple defers accumulate, only execute at function exit
    
    reader := resp.Reader
    defer reader.Close()  // ❌ Same issue - resource leak in retry loop
}
```

**After:**
```go
for attempt := 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++ {
    sp := spinner.New(...)
    sp.Start()
    
    // Properly handle resources immediately when needed
    if err != nil {
        sp.Stop()
        return "", err
    }
    
    // Explicit cleanup with proper error handling
    err = reader.Close()
    sp.Stop()
    if err != nil {
        return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to close reader: %w", err)
    }
}
```

### 🟡 Variable Shadowing Issues
Fixed variable `context` shadowing Go's `context` package in multiple locations:

- `cmd/generate/generate.go`: Renamed `context` to `promptContext` 
- `cmd/generate/context.go`: Renamed `context` to `promptContext` in `CreateContextFromPrompt()`

**Before:**
```go
import "context"

// Creates shadowing issue
context, err := handler.CreateContextFromPrompt()
```

**After:**
```go
import "context"

// No more shadowing
promptContext, err := handler.CreateContextFromPrompt()
```

### 🟢 Code Quality Improvements

b.title: Add `--var` template variable support to `generate` command with command-specific reserved key validation
b.body:
This PR adds `--var` template variable support to the `generate` command, matching the functionality already available in the `run` command. This enables users to create flexible, reusable prompt files for test generation scenarios while preventing conflicts with reserved variables only where necessary.

## Problem

The `generate` command previously only supported a fixed `input` variable when templating prompt files, while the `run` command supported custom template variables via `--var name=value` flags. This inconsistency made it difficult to create reusable prompt templates for test generation.

## Solution

Added complete `--var` template variable support to the `generate` command by:

1. **Added CLI flag support**: The `--var` flag can now be used multiple times to pass custom template variables
2. **Template variable parsing**: Implemented shared `util.ParseTemplateVariables()` function used by both `run` and `generate` commands
3. **Command-specific reserved key validation**: Prevents `input` from being used as a template variable key in the `generate` command only to avoid conflicts with the built-in variable
4. **Pipeline integration**: Template variables are applied during test execution in `runSingleTestWithContext()`
5. **Backward compatibility**: Existing `input` variable is preserved alongside custom variables

## Usage

```bash
# Single variable
gh models generate --var name=Alice prompt.yml

# Multiple variables  
gh models generate --var name=Alice --var topic="machine learning" prompt.yml

# Reserved variable protection (generate command only)
gh models generate --var input=test prompt.yml  # Error: 'input' is a reserved variable name
gh models run --var input=test prompt.yml       # Works fine - input allowed in run command
```

**Example prompt file with template variables:**
```yaml
name: "Customer Support Template"
messages:
  - role: system
    content: "You are a helpful assistant for {{name}}."
  - role: user
    content: "Tell me about {{topic}} in {{style}} style."
```

## Implementation Details

- **Shared utility**: Both `run` and `generate` commands use `util.ParseTemplateVariables()` for consistent behavior
- **Command-specific validation**: Only the `generate` command validates against using "input" as a template variable to prevent conflicts with its built-in variable
- **Template data structure**: `{"input": inputValue, "name": "customValue", ...}`
- **Error handling**: Validates variable format, detects duplicate keys, prevents reserved key usage in generate command only
- **Integration point**: Variables are applied during groundtruth generation when running individual tests

## Testing

- Added comprehensive unit tests for template variable parsing covering various test cases
- Added integration test verifying template variable application in the pipeline
- Added specific test verifying `run` command accepts "input" as template variable
- Added specific test verifying `generate` command rejects "input" as template variable
- All existing tests continue to pass

This change enables more flexible and parameterized prompt files for test generation while maintaining full backward compatibility and preventing variable conflicts only where necessary.

# Rust Backend Rewrite

This PR implements a complete rewrite of the RequestRepo backend and DNS server in Rust, replacing Redis with an in-memory compressed cache while maintaining 1:1 API parity with the existing Python implementation.

## Features Implemented

- **HTTP Server**: Complete implementation of all API endpoints from the original Python backend using axum framework
- **DNS Server**: Full DNS resolver with support for A, AAAA, CNAME, and TXT records using trust-dns-server
- **WebSocket Support**: Real-time updates for request notifications with session management
- **In-Memory Compressed Cache**: Thread-safe cache with compression to replace Redis, including:
  - Key-value operations
  - List operations
  - Pub/sub messaging
  - TTL-based expiration
- **IP Geolocation**: Country tagging for requests using binary search on IP ranges
- **JWT Authentication**: Token-based authentication for API endpoints

## New Features

- **SMTP Logging**: Server listening on port 25 to log email traffic
- **Custom TCP Ports**: Dynamic allocation of TCP ports per session for additional logging capabilities

## Implementation Details

- **Async Runtime**: Uses tokio for high-performance async I/O
- **Thread Safety**: All shared state is protected with appropriate synchronization primitives
- **Compression**: Uses flate2 for efficient data storage
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error handling throughout the codebase
- **Testing**: Unit tests for core functionality

## Benefits

- **Performance**: Significant performance improvements due to Rust's efficiency
- **Memory Usage**: Reduced memory footprint with compressed storage
- **Reliability**: Strong type system and ownership model prevent many classes of bugs

a.title: Fix `func pack` command for C# in-process projects and add basic functionality tests for other languages
a.body:
The `func pack` command was failing for C# in-process projects with the error "Pack command doesn't work for dotnet functions", while the same projects worked fine with `func azure functionapp publish`. This inconsistency made it impossible to create deployment packages manually for C# in-process projects.

I've also added E2E tests that test the basic functionality for `func pack` for the other worker runtimes.

## Root Cause
The issue was in `PackAction.cs` where the call to `ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile()` was missing the `ignoreDotNetCheck: true` parameter. This caused the following condition in `ZipHelper.cs` to evaluate to `true` and throw an exception:

```csharp
if (GlobalCoreToolsSettings.CurrentWorkerRuntime == WorkerRuntime.Dotnet && 
    !ignoreDotNetCheck && !noBuild && buildOption != BuildOption.Remote)
{
    throw new CliException("Pack command doesn't work for dotnet functions");
}
```

## Solution
Updated `PackAction.cs` to pass `ignoreDotNetCheck: true` to match the pattern used in `PublishFunctionAppAction.cs`:

**Before:**
```csharp
var stream = await ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile(functionAppRoot, BuildNativeDeps, 
    noBuild: false, buildOption: BuildOption.Default, additionalPackages: AdditionalPackages);
```

**After:**
```csharp
var stream = await ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile(functionAppRoot, BuildNativeDeps, BuildOption.Default, 
    noBuild: false, ignoreParser: null, AdditionalPackages, ignoreDotNetCheck: true);
```

## Testing
- Added unit test `PackActionTests.cs` to verify the exception is no longer thrown
- Added E2E test `DotnetInProcessPackTests.cs` for full workflow validation
- Verified the fix follows the same pattern as the working publish functionality

This change allows C# in-process projects to use `func pack` successfully, matching the behavior already available for C# isolated projects and the publish command.

Fixes #3623.

b.title: Add automatic remote build detection for Python apps in func pack command
b.body:
## Summary

This PR implements automatic remote build detection for the `func pack` command when running Python function apps on Windows machines that target Linux environments. This addresses the cross-platform scenario where Python dependencies need to be built for the correct target platform.

## Problem

Previously, the `func pack` command always used local builds regardless of the development platform, which could cause issues when:
- Developing Python function apps on Windows 
- The function app targets Linux (typical for Azure Functions Python runtime)
- Dependencies in `requirements.txt` contain native code that needs to be compiled for Linux

This resulted in Windows-compiled dependencies being packaged, which would fail when deployed to Linux-based Azure Functions.

## Solution

Extended the existing remote build detection logic from the `func azure functionapp publish` command to the `func pack` command:

### Changes Made

1. **PackAction.cs**: Modified to automatically resolve build options instead of using hardcoded `BuildOption.Default`
   ```csharp
   // Before
   var stream = await ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile(functionAppRoot, BuildNativeDeps, noBuild: false, buildOption: BuildOption.Default, additionalPackages: AdditionalPackages);
   
   // After  
   var buildOption = PublishHelper.ResolveBuildOption(BuildOption.Default, workerRuntime, site: null, BuildNativeDeps, noBuild: false);
   var stream = await ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile(functionAppRoot, BuildNativeDeps, noBuild: false, buildOption: buildOption, additionalPackages: AdditionalPackages);
   ```

### Behavior

The `func pack` command will now automatically use remote build when:
- ✅ Worker runtime is Python
- ✅ `requirements.txt` exists and has content  

All other scenarios maintain existing behavior:
- ❌ Non-Python runtimes → Default build
- ❌ No `requirements.txt` → Default build  
- ❌ Empty `requirements.txt` → Default build
- ❌ Explicit `--build-native-deps` flags → Respect user choice

### Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests covering:
- Python apps with/without `requirements.txt`
- Different worker runtimes (Python, Node.js, etc.)
- Build option precedence and edge cases
- File system scenarios with temporary test directories

## Benefits

- **Seamless cross-platform development**: Python developers on Windows get correct Linux-compatible packages automatically
- **No breaking changes**: Existing behavior maintained for all other scenarios
- **Consistent with publish command**: Uses same logic as `func azure functionapp publish`
- **No additional flags required**: Works automatically based on project detection

Fixes #4255.

b.title: Create pipeline to validate DBX JSON certificate references
b.body:
This PR implements a validation pipeline to ensure that DBX JSON files reference certificate files that actually exist in the `PreSignedObjects/DBX/Certificates` folder.

## Problem
When new DBX JSON files are created, the internal certificate names referenced in the JSON don't always match the external filenames in the Certificates folder, and there was no validation to catch these mismatches. For example, the current `dbx_info_msft_06_10_25.json` references `WindowsProduction2011.cer` but the actual file is named `MicWinProPCA2011_2011-10-19.der`.

## Solution
Added a new validation script and CI pipeline step that:

1. **Finds the latest DBX JSON file** - Automatically locates `dbx_info_msft_<date>.json` files
2. **Validates certificate references** - Checks that all certificates listed in the "certificates" array actually exist in the Certificates folder
3. **Provides clear error messages** - Shows exactly which certificates are missing and lists available files for debugging
4. **Handles edge cases** - Gracefully handles missing certificates sections, malformed JSON, etc.

## Changes Made

### New Files
- `scripts/validate_dbx_references.py` - Main validation script with CLI interface
- `scripts/test_validate_dbx_references.py` - Comprehensive unit tests (7 test cases)

### CI Integration  
- Added validation step to `.github/workflows/prepare-binaries.yml` after unit tests
- Pipeline will now fail on PR/release if certificate references are invalid

### Other
- Fixed `.gitignore` to properly exclude `__pycache__` directories
- Removed accidentally committed cache files

## Testing
```bash
# Current mismatch is detected
$ python scripts/validate_dbx_references.py PreSignedObjects/DBX
ERROR: Certificate file 'WindowsProduction2011.cer' referenced in JSON but not found in PreSignedObjects/DBX/Certificates
INFO: Available certificate files:
INFO:   - MicWinProPCA2011_2011-10-19.der

# All unit tests pass
$ pytest scripts/test_validate_dbx_references.py
7 passed in 0.01s
```

The validation script successfully detects the existing mismatch and will prevent similar issues in the future through automated CI checks.

a.title: feat: enable IPv6 dual-stack on aggregator services
a.body:
## Problem

When setting `enabledIPv6: true` for FluentD or Syslog-NG, the process correctly listens on IPv6, but the Kubernetes Service resources are not configured for dual-stack networking. This prevents proper IPv6 connectivity to these services in dual-stack Kubernetes clusters.

## Solution

This PR adds automatic dual-stack configuration to all FluentD and Syslog-NG Kubernetes Services when `enabledIPv6: true` is set in their respective specs.

## Changes Made

### FluentD IPv6 Support

Modified the FluentD service reconciler (`pkg/resources/fluentd/service.go`) to configure the following when `enabledIPv6` is enabled:

- `ipFamilyPolicy: PreferDualStack` - Allows services to work on both single-stack and dual-stack clusters
- `ipFamilies: [IPv4, IPv6]` - Configures dual-stack with IPv4 as primary protocol

All FluentD services now support dual-stack when IPv6 is enabled:
- Main service (`fluentd`)
- Headless service (`fluentd-headless`)
- Metrics service (`fluentd-metrics`)
- Buffer metrics service (`fluentd-buffer-metrics`)

### Syslog-NG IPv6 Support

Added `EnabledIPv6` field to `SyslogNGSpec` in `pkg/sdk/logging/api/v1beta1/syslogng_types.go` and modified the Syslog-NG service reconciler (`pkg/resources/syslogng/service.go`) with the same dual-stack configuration as FluentD.

All Syslog-NG services now support dual-stack when IPv6 is enabled:
- Main service (`syslog-ng`)
- Headless service (`syslog-ng-headless`)
- Metrics service (`syslog-ng-metrics`)
- Buffer metrics service (`syslog-ng-buffer-metrics`)

### Generated Files

Generated CRD YAML files and documentation to reflect the new `enabledIPv6` field in SyslogNGSpec:
- Updated Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions
- Generated API documentation for syslog-ng types

## Example

Before this change, enabling IPv6 only configured the process:

```yaml
apiVersion: logging.banzaicloud.io/v1beta1
kind: Logging
metadata:
  name: default-logging
spec:
  fluentd:
    enabledIPv6: true
  syslogNG:
    enabledIPv6: true
```

This resulted in services that only had IPv4 cluster IPs, preventing IPv6 connectivity.

After this change, the services are automatically configured for dual-stack:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: fluentd
spec:
  ipFamilyPolicy: PreferDualStack
  ipFamilies:
    - IPv4
    - IPv6
  # ... rest of service spec
```

## Backward Compatibility

The `PreferDualStack` policy ensures backward compatibility:
- On single-stack IPv4 clusters: Services work as before with only IPv4
- On dual-stack clusters: Services get both IPv4 and IPv6 cluster IPs
- No breaking changes to existing configurations

The changes preserve existing ClusterIPs during updates for proper dual-stack operation.

Fixes kube-logging/logging-operator#2100

a.title: Enhance branch selection UI with search and better ordering using real repository data
a.body:
The branch selection UI in the import dialog was problematic for repositories with many branches, using a simple dropdown that would become unwieldy and lack search functionality. This PR completely overhauls the branch selection experience with a modern, scalable interface that uses only authentic repository data.

## Key Improvements

### 🔍 Search Functionality
Added a real-time search bar that filters branches as you type, making it easy to find specific branches in repositories with dozens or hundreds of branches.

### 📊 Smart Branch Ordering
Implemented intelligent branch ordering where:
- Default branch appears first with a "Default" badge
- Main/master branches get priority positioning  
- Remaining branches are sorted alphabetically
- Visual indicators clearly identify special branches

### 🎨 Scrollable Dropdown Design
Replaced the cramped simple dropdown with a scrollable container (max-height: 240px) that can handle unlimited branches without breaking the UI layout.

### ✨ Enhanced User Experience
- **Click-outside to close**: Dropdown closes when clicking elsewhere
- **Clear search button**: Quick X button to reset search
- **Branch count footer**: Shows "X of Y branches shown" for filtered results
- **Empty state handling**: Proper messages for no branches or no search results
- **Loading states**: Smooth loading indicators and error handling

### 🔒 Authentic Data Only
Removed all dummy/demo branch data to ensure the UI only displays actual branches from the connected repository:
- No hardcoded fallback branches
- No demo data when repository has no branches
- Pure repository API integration for authentic user experience

## Technical Implementation

The enhancement focuses on the `FileChatInterface.tsx` component where the branch import dialog is rendered. Key additions include:

- `branchSearchQuery` state for real-time search filtering
- `getFilteredAndSortedBranches()` helper function for intelligent ordering with real data only
- `getBranchDisplayInfo()` helper for branch metadata and visual indicators
- Enhanced dropdown UI with search bar, scrollable list, and footer stats
- Removed dummy branch arrays and fallback data

a.title: Fix DEP0190 deprecation warning in Azure CLI credential
a.body:
This PR fixes the Node.js DEP0190 deprecation warning that occurs when using `AzureCliCredential` with Node.js v24+.

## Issue
The `getAzureCliAccessToken` method was calling `child_process.execFile` with `shell: true`, which triggers Node.js deprecation warning DEP0190:

```
(node:1252) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities, as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.
```

## Solution
Removed the `shell: true` option from the `execFile` call. This approach:

1. **Eliminates the deprecation warning** - `execFile` without shell is the recommended secure approach
2. **Maintains functionality** - All existing behavior is preserved as verified by comprehensive test suite
3. **Improves security** - Avoids potential argument injection vulnerabilities
4. **Aligns with existing patterns** - `AzureDeveloperCliCredential` already uses this approach successfully

## Changes
- **Source**: Removed `shell: true` from `execFile` options in `azureCliCredential.ts`
- **Tests**: Updated test expectations to check for `shell: undefined` instead of `shell: true`
- **Impact**: Minimal change (1 line in source, 16 lines in tests)

## Verification
- ✅ All existing tests pass
- ✅ Build succeeds
- ✅ Linting passes
- ✅ No functional changes to credential behavior

b.title: Add 410 status code handling to ManagedIdentityCredential retry policy with 70-second minimum duration
b.body:
## Summary

This PR implements handling for HTTP 410 (Gone) status responses in the ManagedIdentityCredential retry policy to meet Azure IMDS service requirements for at least 70 seconds total retry duration.

## Problem

The current `imdsRetryPolicy` only retries on 404 status codes, but according to [Azure IMDS documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/instance-metadata-service?tabs=windows#errors-and-debugging), 410 status codes can also be returned when the identity is still being set up and require special handling with sufficient retry duration.

## Solution

Following the .NET SDK implementation approach, this PR:

1. **Adds 410 status code to retry logic** alongside existing 404 handling
2. **Enforces minimum 3-second initial delay** for 410 responses to ensure at least 70 seconds total retry duration
3. **Preserves existing behavior** for 404 responses and all other scenarios

### Technical Implementation

```typescript
// For 410 responses, use minimum 3-second delay to ensure at least 70 seconds total retry duration
const initialDelayMs = response?.status === 410 
  ? Math.max(MIN_DELAY_FOR_410_MS, msiRetryConfig.startDelayInMs)
  : msiRetryConfig.startDelayInMs;
```

The 3-second minimum is calculated based on exponential backoff with 5 retries:
- Delays: d, 2d, 4d, 8d, 16d = 31d total
- With jitter (80% minimum): 31d × 0.8 ≥ 70 seconds
- Therefore: d ≥ 2.82 seconds, using 3 seconds for safety

## Validation

✅ **410 responses**: Retry with 3-second minimum delay, achieving 70+ second total duration  
✅ **404 responses**: Continue using configured delay (unchanged behavior)  
✅ **Other status codes**: No retries (unchanged behavior)

b.title: Fix piping query without `go` command into sqlcmd-go
b.body:
## Issue
When piping a SQL query to sqlcmd-go without a `GO` statement, the query was read but not executed, returning no output. However, the ODBC version of sqlcmd does execute these queries.

For example:
```
# Returns nothing in sqlcmd-go (before fix)
$ cat query.sql | sqlcmd-go

# Works correctly in ODBC version
$ cat query.sql | sqlcmd-odbc
master
tempdb
model
msdb
...
```

## Root Cause
The issue was in the `run` function in `cmd/sqlcmd/sqlcmd.go`. When input is coming from stdin in non-interactive mode, the `processAll` parameter was always set to `false`. This meant that when EOF was reached, if there was no explicit `GO` statement, the query would not be executed.

## Solution
The fix detects when stdin is a pipe (not an interactive terminal) and sets `processAll=true` in that case, which executes the query when EOF is reached:

```go
iactive := args.InputFile == nil && args.Query == ""
if iactive || s.Query != "" {
    processAll := false
    if iactive {
        // Check if stdin is a pipe rather than a terminal
        fi, _ := os.Stdin.Stat()
        if fi != nil && (fi.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice) == 0 {
            // Stdin is not a terminal, it's being piped in
            processAll = true
        }
    }
    err = s.Run(once, processAll)
}
```

This minimal change ensures that sqlcmd-go behaves like the ODBC version when receiving piped input, executing queries without requiring a `GO` statement.

Fixes #581.

b.title: Fix infinite loop and prevent control operations when TRV becomes unavailable
b.body:
## Problem

Users reported that Home Assistant would completely freeze and become unresponsive when turning the HVAC mode from "off" to "heating". The issue occurred randomly and required a forced shutdown of the system.

### Root Cause

The freeze was caused by an infinite loop in the control queue when TRV (Thermostatic Radiator Valve) entities became unavailable:

1. When `get_current_offset()` was called in various adapters, it attempted to convert the entity state to a float
2. When the TRV was unavailable (e.g., network issue, device offline), the state was the string `'unavailable'`
3. This caused a `ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'unavailable'`
4. The exception was caught in `control_queue()`, which set `result = False` and retried the task
5. Since the TRV was still unavailable, the same error occurred again, creating an infinite loop
6. This loop blocked the MainThread, causing Home Assistant to freeze completely

Additionally, when TRVs became unavailable, Better Thermostat would still attempt to perform control operations (set temperature, set HVAC mode, set offset), which could cause AttributeErrors and failed service calls.

From the error logs:
```python
File "/config/custom_components/better_thermostat/adapters/generic.py", line 56, in get_current_offset
    return float(str(state))
ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'unavailable'
```

## Solution

Implemented a two-layer protection approach:

### Layer 1: Adapter State Validation

Added state validation in all adapter `get_current_offset()` methods to check if the entity state is unavailable or unknown before attempting float conversion:

```python
async def get_current_offset(self, entity_id):
    """Get current offset."""
    state = self.hass.states.get(entity_id)
    if state is None or state.state in (STATE_UNAVAILABLE, STATE_UNKNOWN):
        return None  # Gracefully handle unavailable state
    return float(str(state.attributes.get("offset", 0)))
```

When `None` is returned, the existing error handling in `controlling.py` gracefully handles it by logging an error and exiting the control cycle successfully.

### Layer 2: Control Logic Protection

Added early state check in `control_trv()` to detect unavailable TRVs before attempting any control operations:

```python
# Check if TRV is available before attempting to control it
if _trv is None or _trv.state in (STATE_UNAVAILABLE, STATE_UNKNOWN):
    _LOGGER.warning(
        "better_thermostat %s: TRV %s is unavailable, skipping control cycle",
        self.device_name,
        heater_entity_id,
    )
    self.ignore_states = False
    self.real_trvs[heater_entity_id]["ignore_trv_states"] = False
    return True
```

This prevents:
- AttributeError when accessing unavailable TRV attributes
- Attempting to set temperature on unavailable TRVs
- Attempting to set HVAC mode on unavailable TRVs
- Attempting to set calibration offset on unavailable TRVs

## Changes

- **generic.py**: Added state validation for local temperature calibration entity
- **deconz.py**: Added state validation for DeCONZ thermostat entity
- **mqtt.py**: Added state validation for MQTT thermostat entity
- **tado.py**: Added state validation for Tado thermostat entity
- **controlling.py**: Added early TRV availability check before attempting control operations

## Impact

- ✅ Prevents Home Assistant from freezing when TRV entities become unavailable
- ✅ Prevents AttributeError and failed service calls on unavailable TRVs
- ✅ Logs warnings for visibility when TRVs are unavailable
- ✅ Backward compatible - no breaking changes to existing functionality
- ✅ Self-healing - automatically resumes normal operation when TRV comes back online
- ✅ Comprehensive fix across all adapter types (generic, deconz, mqtt, tado)
- ✅ Minimal code changes - only affected functions modified

## Testing

- Python syntax validation passed
- Black code formatter compliance verified
- Flake8 linting passed with no errors
- Tested scenarios: unavailable, unknown, None, and valid float values

## Description

This PR adds the missing `refreshControl` PropType definition to the BigList component.

## Problem

The BigList component's render method uses `this.props.refreshControl` to allow users to pass a custom RefreshControl component:

```javascript
const defaultProps = {
  refreshControl:
    onRefresh && !this.props.refreshControl ? (
      <RefreshControl refreshing={refreshing} onRefresh={onRefresh} />
    ) : null,

};
```

However, the PropTypes definition was missing this prop, which could cause PropTypes validation warnings when users pass a custom `refreshControl` to the component.

## Solution

Added `refreshControl: PropTypes.element` to the `BigList.propTypes` definition, placed logically right after the `refreshing` prop since they are related.

## Usage

The BigList component now properly validates both ways of using pull-to-refresh functionality:

**Option 1: Auto-generated RefreshControl**
```jsx
<BigList
  data={data}
  itemHeight={50}
  renderItem={renderItem}
  onRefresh={handleRefresh}

<BigList
  data={data}
  itemHeight={50}
  renderItem={renderItem}
  refreshControl={
    <RefreshControl
      refreshing={isRefreshing}
      onRefresh={handleRefresh}
      tintColor="red"

/>
```

## Changes

b.title: Add Len() method to CDC FIFO queue using BoltDB bucket Stats()
b.body:
This PR adds a `Len()` method to the CDC FIFO queue that returns the number of items currently stored in the queue. The implementation uses BoltDB's bucket `Stats()` method to get an accurate count via `BucketStats.KeyN`.

## Implementation Details

The new method follows the existing thread-safe query pattern used by other queue methods like `Empty()`, `HasNext()`, and `HighestKey()`:

```go
// Len returns the number of items currently in the queue.
func (q *Queue) Len() int {
    req := queryReq{respChan: make(chan queryResp)}
    q.queryChan <- req
    resp := <-req.respChan
    return resp.len
}
```

The implementation:
- Uses `bucket.Stats().KeyN` from BoltDB to get the actual key count
- Integrates seamlessly with the existing single-goroutine query handling pattern
- Maintains thread safety by routing requests through the queue's main goroutine
- Adds minimal overhead by extending the existing query response structure

## Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests that verify:
- Empty queue returns length 0
- Adding items increases length correctly (1, then 2)
- Reading from events channel doesn't affect length (items remain in database)
- `DeleteRange()` operations correctly reduce the length
- Batch operations with multiple items work correctly

All existing tests continue to pass, ensuring no regressions.

a.title: Fix goal target progress calculation for equal from/to values
a.body:
Goal targets with equal 'from' and 'to' values were incorrectly showing 100% completion instead of 0% completion, creating a confusing user experience.

## Problem

When users create goal targets where the start and target values are the same (e.g., "from 0 to 0 signups"), the system would display 100% completion even when the current value matches the target. This is misleading because there's no actual progress to be made when the start and end points are identical.

![Goal target showing 100% completion for "from 0 to 0 signups"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f800f101-647c-4d7c-bcc6-98ddba774311)

## Solution

Updated the progress calculation logic across three key locations to return 0% completion when `from == to`:

- **Frontend TypeScript model** (`app/assets/js/models/goals/index.tsx`)
- **TurboUI component** (`turboui/src/GoalTargetList/index.tsx`) 
- **Elixir backend** (`app/lib/operately/goals/target.ex`)

The fix ensures that targets with equal start/end values display 0% progress, which is more intuitive and less confusing for users who may set such values while drafting their goals.

## Additional Fix

b.title: Fix GoldMaster configuration: replace optimize "Full" with "Speed" for Xcode compatibility
b.body:
This PR addresses a build compatibility issue with newer versions of Xcode where the `-OFull` optimization flag has been deprecated. The issue was causing build failures on macOS when using the GoldMaster configuration.

## Problem
The premake lua scripts throughout the codebase were using `optimize "Full"` in GoldMaster configuration blocks, which translates to the deprecated `-OFull` compiler flag in newer Xcode versions.

## Solution
Updated all instances of `optimize "Full"` to `optimize "Speed"` in GoldMaster configuration blocks across 17 lua files. The new configuration follows the pattern:

```lua
filter "configurations:GoldMaster"
    defines { "RAZIX_GOLD_MASTER", "NDEBUG" }
    symbols "Off"
    runtime "Release"
    optimize "Speed"  -- Changed from "Full" to "Speed"
```

## Files Modified
- Core engine and framework files: `razix_engine.lua`, `razix_game_framework.lua`
- Sandbox and test configurations: `sandbox.lua`, test lua files
- All vendor library configurations (17 files total including GLFW, Jolt, ImGui, Tracy, SPIRV libraries, etc.)

## Impact
This change ensures compatibility with newer Xcode versions while maintaining equivalent optimization performance. The `Speed` optimization level provides similar performance characteristics to the deprecated `Full` level.

Fixes #447.

a.title: Fix StackOverflowError in WxCpRedissonConfigImpl and WxCpRedisTemplateConfigImpl toString() methods
a.body:
## Problem

When initializing `WxCpRedissonConfigImpl` or `WxCpRedisTemplateConfigImpl` objects, calling `toString()` (either explicitly or during debugging/logging) results in a `StackOverflowError`. This occurs because:

1. These classes inherit the `toString()` method from `WxCpDefaultConfigImpl`
2. The inherited method uses `WxCpGsonBuilder.create().toJson(this)` to serialize the entire object
3. GSON attempts to serialize the `redisOps` field containing complex Redis client objects (`RedissonClient` or `StringRedisTemplate`)
4. These Redis client objects have circular references or complex object graphs that cause GSON to enter an infinite recursion loop

```java
// This code throws StackOverflowError
WxCpRedissonConfigImpl config = new WxCpRedissonConfigImpl(redissonClient, "workRedis:");
config.setCorpId("testCorp");
config.setAgentId(1000);
String result = config.toString(); // StackOverflowError here
```

## Solution

Added a custom `toString()` method in `AbstractWxCpInRedisConfigImpl` that provides a safe implementation excluding the problematic Redis client objects:

```java
@Override
public String toString() {
  return "AbstractWxCpInRedisConfigImpl{" +
    "corpId='" + getCorpId() + '\'' +
    ", agentId=" + getAgentId() +
    ", keyPrefix='" + keyPrefix + '\'' +
    ", accessTokenKey='" + accessTokenKey + '\'' +
    ", jsapiTicketKey='" + jsapiTicketKey + '\'' +
    ", agentJsapiTicketKey='" + agentJsapiTicketKey + '\'' +
    ", lockKey='" + lockKey + '\'' +
    '}';
}
```

## Benefits

- ✅ **Resolves StackOverflowError**: No more infinite recursion when calling toString()
- ✅ **Preserves debugging information**: Shows all relevant configuration details
- ✅ **Safe and reliable**: Uses simple string concatenation instead of complex GSON serialization  
- ✅ **Minimal change**: Only 13 lines added, no existing functionality modified
- ✅ **Affects both implementations**: Fixes the issue for both `WxCpRedissonConfigImpl` and `WxCpRedisTemplateConfigImpl`

## Testing

The fix has been verified to work correctly:

```
AbstractWxCpInRedisConfigImpl{corpId='testCorpId', agentId=1001, keyPrefix='demo:', accessTokenKey='demo:wechat_cp_access_token_key:testCorpId:1001', jsapiTicketKey='demo:wechat_cp_jsapi_ticket_key:testCorpId:1001', agentJsapiTicketKey='demo:wechat_cp_agent_jsapi_ticket_key:testCorpId:1001', lockKey='demo:wechat_cp_lock:testCorpId:1001'}
```

Fixes #3644.

b.title: Implement HTTP connection pooling for WxPayServiceApacheHttpImpl
b.body:
This PR implements HTTP connection pooling for `WxPayServiceApacheHttpImpl` to address performance issues caused by creating new HttpClient instances for each request.

## Problem
The current implementation creates a new `HttpClient` for every HTTP request:
```java
HttpClientBuilder httpClientBuilder = this.createHttpClientBuilder(useKey);
try (CloseableHttpClient httpClient = httpClientBuilder.build()) {
    // Make request and close client
}
```

This approach causes:
- Unnecessary overhead from frequent connection establishment/teardown
- Poor performance in high-concurrency scenarios
- Inefficient resource utilization

## Solution
Implemented connection pooling using Apache HttpClient's `PoolingHttpClientConnectionManager`:

### Key Changes
1. **Added connection pool configuration to WxPayConfig**:
   - `maxConnTotal` (default: 20) - Maximum total connections
   - `maxConnPerRoute` (default: 10) - Maximum connections per route
   - Separate pooled clients for SSL and non-SSL requests

2. **Enhanced WxPayConfig with pooled client initialization**:
   ```java
   public CloseableHttpClient initHttpClient() throws WxPayException
   public CloseableHttpClient initSslHttpClient() throws WxPayException
   ```

3. **Modified request methods to use pooled clients**:
   ```java
   CloseableHttpClient httpClient = this.createHttpClient(useKey);
   // Reuse pooled client instead of creating new one
   ```

### Features
- **Backward Compatible**: Zero breaking changes, existing code works without modification
- **SSL Support**: Separate connection pool for SSL requests with proper certificate handling
- **Proxy Support**: Maintains existing proxy configuration functionality
- **Customizable**: Supports existing `HttpClientBuilderCustomizer` interface
- **Configurable**: Adjustable pool size parameters

### Performance Benefits
- Eliminates per-request HttpClient creation overhead
- Enables HTTP connection reuse and keep-alive
- Better resource management for high-concurrency applications
- Improved scalability for payment processing workflows

### Usage
Connection pooling is automatically enabled with sensible defaults:
```java
WxPayConfig config = new WxPayConfig();
config.setMaxConnTotal(50);      // Optional: customize max connections
config.setMaxConnPerRoute(20);   // Optional: customize per-route limit

WxPayServiceApacheHttpImpl payService = new WxPayServiceApacheHttpImpl();
payService.setConfig(config);
// All requests now use connection pooling automatically
```

Fixes #3640.

a.title: Fix tryTo steps appearing in test failure traces
a.body:
When using `tryTo` to handle optional/flaky steps, failed steps inside `tryTo` were incorrectly appearing in the main test failure trace, even when the actual test failure occurred from a different step later in the test.

**Example of the issue:**

```javascript
Scenario('test something', async ({ I }) => {
  I.amOnPage('https://codecept.io/quickstart/')
  
  // This step fails but should be handled gracefully by tryTo
  const result = await tryTo(() => { I.seeElement('.doesntexist') })
  
  I.fillField('#algolia-search-input', 'codecept')
  I.pressKey('Enter')
  I.see('CodeceptJS')
  
  // This is the actual failing step
  I.seeCheckboxIsChecked('.nocheckboxishere')
});
```

**Before the fix:** The error trace would show the failed `I.seeElement('.doesntexist')` step from inside `tryTo` as part of the failure trace, confusing developers about the actual source of the test failure.

**After the fix:** Only steps executed outside of `tryTo` and `hopeThat` sessions are included in the main test failure trace, providing a cleaner and more accurate representation of what actually caused the test to fail.

**Implementation:** Modified the step recording logic in `lib/listener/steps.js` to exclude steps from `tryTo` and `hopeThat` sessions when building the main test steps array. Added comprehensive unit tests to validate the behavior.

Fixes #4619.

a.title: Fix incorrect JOIN/ON clause reconstruction
a.body:
## Problem

When parsing SQL statements with multiple JOIN clauses, the reconstructed SQL string (`Statement.String()`) incorrectly ordered the JOIN and ON clauses. For example:

```diff
- FROM worker w
- JOIN event_worker ew ON ew.worker_id = w."id"
- JOIN sys_event se ON se."id" = ew."event"
+ FROM "worker" AS "w"
+ JOIN "event_worker" AS "ew"
+ JOIN "sys_event" AS "se" ON "se"."id" = "ew"."event"
+ ON "ew"."worker_id" = "w"."id"
```

The issue was in how the `JoinClause.String()` method handled nested JOIN clauses created by the parser.

## Solution

This PR updates the `JoinClause.String()` method to correctly handle the nested structure of JOIN clauses built by the parser. The solution specifically:

1. Handles simple JOINs with a constraint
2. Handles a single level of nested JOINs
3. Handles double-nested JOINs for more complex queries

The changes are minimal and focused on just the `JoinClause.String()` method. Comprehensive tests were added to verify correct reconstruction of:
- Basic multiple JOINs with ON constraints
- Complex queries with three or more tables
- Mixed JOIN types (LEFT JOIN, INNER JOIN, CROSS JOIN)

## Example

The reconstructed SQL now correctly maintains the proper ordering of JOIN and ON clauses:

```sql
SELECT * FROM "worker" AS "w" JOIN "event_worker" AS "ew" ON "ew"."worker_id" = "w"."id" JOIN "sys_event" AS "se" ON "se"."id" = "ew"."event"
```

Fixes #47.

b.title: Add support for schema.table syntax in CREATE TABLE statements
b.body:
This PR adds support for SQLite's schema-qualified table names in CREATE TABLE statements.

## Problem

SQLite allows prefixing table names with a schema name using the `schema.table` syntax, particularly with the built-in schemas `main` and `temp`. For example:

```sql
CREATE TABLE main.users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)
```

However, the parser currently expects either a parenthesis or "AS" after the table name, causing an error when it encounters a dot:

```
error: 1:18: expected AS or left paren, found '.'
```

## Changes

1. Added a `Schema` field to the `CreateTableStatement` struct to store the optional schema name
2. Modified the parser to check for and handle the schema.table syntax in CREATE TABLE statements
3. Updated the `Clone()` and `String()` methods to properly handle the new Schema field
4. Added tests to verify both schema.table syntax and backward compatibility

## Example

Now both of these statements parse correctly:

```sql
-- With schema prefix
CREATE TABLE main.T1 (C1 TEXT PRIMARY KEY, C2 INTEGER)

-- Without schema prefix (backward compatible)
CREATE TABLE T2 (C1 TEXT PRIMARY KEY, C2 INTEGER)
```

The parser correctly identifies:
- `main` as the schema and `T1` as the table name in the first example
- `T2` as just the table name (with no schema) in the second example

Fixes #31.

The existing CODEOWNERS file provides equivalent or better reviewer coverage:

- **Default rule**: `* @azure/azure-sdn-members` covers all directories that previously had `reviewers: - "azure/azure-sdn-members"`
- **Specific rules**: `/dropgz/` and `/zapai/` have their own targeted reviewers, providing even more precise assignments than the generic team assignment

## Background

According to GitHub's [blog post](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-04-29-dependabot-reviewers-configuration-option-being-replaced-by-code-owners/), the `reviewers` field in dependabot.yml files will be removed soon, and GitHub will automatically use the CODEOWNERS file to determine reviewers for Dependabot PRs.

This change ensures our repository remains compliant with the upcoming changes while maintaining the same reviewer assignment functionality.

Fixes #3714.

b.title: Update Dependabot version constraints for Kubernetes dependencies compatibility
b.body:
This PR adds version constraints to the Dependabot configuration to ensure Kubernetes dependencies remain compatible with versions 1.30, 1.31, and 1.32.

## Problem
Without version constraints, Dependabot could automatically update Kubernetes dependencies to v0.33.x or higher, which would correspond to Kubernetes 1.33+ and potentially break compatibility with the supported Kubernetes version range.

## Solution
Added `ignore` constraints to all `gomod` package ecosystem entries in `.github/dependabot.yaml` to prevent updates beyond the compatibility range:

### Kubernetes Dependencies Constrained:
- `k8s.io/api` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0
- `k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0  
- `k8s.io/apimachinery` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0
- `k8s.io/client-go` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0
- `k8s.io/kubelet` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0
- `k8s.io/kubectl` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0

### Directories Updated:
- Main repository root (`/`)
- Azure IPAM directory (`/azure-ipam`)
- Build tools directory (`/build/tools`)
- Azure NPM to Cilium validator (`/tools/azure-npm-to-cilium-validator`) - newly added entry
- Release/v1.5 branch entries (both root and azure-ipam)
- Release/v1.4 branch entries (both root and azure-ipam)

### Version Mapping:
- v0.30.x = Kubernetes 1.30.x ✅ (allowed)
- v0.31.x = Kubernetes 1.31.x ✅ (allowed) 
- v0.32.x = Kubernetes 1.32.x ✅ (allowed)
- v0.33.x = Kubernetes 1.33.x ❌ (ignored)

## Testing
- ✅ YAML syntax validated
- ✅ Build successful with no functional changes
- ✅ All directories containing k8s.io dependencies are covered

The constraints ensure Dependabot will only propose updates within the compatible Kubernetes version range while allowing patch and minor version updates within the supported major versions.

Fixes #3726.

a.title: Cache hub_client.beta.threads.messages.list in environment.py
a.body:
The `hub_client.beta.threads.messages.list` API call was taking a long time to run and being called repeatedly during agent execution, causing performance issues.

This PR implements a message cache in the `Environment` class that:

- **Caches messages on first call**: The first `_list_messages()` call fetches from the API and populates the cache
- **Serves subsequent calls from cache**: Following calls return cached data instantly without API requests
- **Updates cache on new messages**: `add_reply()` and `_add_message()` automatically append new messages to the cache
- **Invalidates cache at run end**: Cache is cleared when agent runs complete to ensure fresh data for next execution

## Implementation Details

```python
# Cache structure added to Environment.__init__()
self._messages_cache: Optional[List[Message]] = None
self._messages_cache_initialized = False

# Cache-aware message listing
def _list_messages(limit, order, thread_id):
    if cache_available_for_thread:
        return cached_messages  # Instant return
    
    # Fetch from API and populate cache
    messages = hub_client.beta.threads.messages.list(...)
    self._messages_cache = messages.data
    return messages.data

# Cache updates on new messages  
def add_reply(message):
    new_message = hub_client.beta.threads.messages.create(...)
    if cache_initialized:
        self._messages_cache.append(new_message)  # Keep cache in sync
    return new_message
```

## Performance Impact

- **First API call per run**: Normal performance (cache miss)
- **Subsequent calls in same run**: Instant response (cache hit)
- **Memory usage**: Minimal - only stores messages for current thread
- **Thread safety**: Cache only applies to main thread, other threads bypass cache

## Cache Lifecycle

1. **Initialization**: Cache starts empty and uninitialized
2. **Population**: First `_list_messages()` call loads cache from API
3. **Updates**: New messages automatically added to cache via `add_reply()`
4. **Invalidation**: Cache cleared in `run()` method's finally block

The implementation respects thread boundaries and maintains data consistency while providing significant performance improvements for repeated message list operations during agent execution.

Fixes #1178.

b.title: Implement asynchronous API calls for file and message creation in environment.py
b.body:
This PR addresses the performance issue where API calls to create messages and files were taking too long by implementing asynchronous execution with concurrent processing.

## Problem
When agents make multiple tool calls or create multiple files, the synchronous API calls were executed sequentially, causing significant delays:
- 5 tool calls × 200ms each = 1000ms total execution time
- Multiple file uploads processed one at a time
- Poor user experience due to high latency

## Solution
Added comprehensive async support while maintaining full backward compatibility:

### Concurrent Execution
- Tool call responses now created concurrently using `asyncio`

### Configuration & Fallback
- New `ASYNC_API_CALLS` environment variable (default: `true`)

## Backward Compatibility
- ✅ All original synchronous methods preserved unchanged
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing API
- ✅ Opt-in async execution via environment variable

## Usage
```bash
# Enable async API calls (default)
export ASYNC_API_CALLS=true

# Disable if needed
export ASYNC_API_CALLS=false
```

Fixes #1180.
